ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a square, with vertices labeled P, V, R, Q, where P is at the upper left, V is at the upper right, R is at the lower right, and Q is at the lower left. Inside the square is drawn triangle PVW, whose base is the upper side PV of the square, and point W is inside the square. On the right side there is a regular pentagon VUTSR, which shares side VR with the square, with point U above and to the right of V, T on the right side, and S below and to the right. Reasoning: Because PVRQ is a square, PV = VR, and ∠PVR = 90°. Because PVW is an equilateral triangle, VW = PV, and ∠PVW = 60°. Because VUTSR is a regular pentagon and shares side VR, VU = VR, and each interior angle of a regular pentagon is 108°, so at point V, the interior angle between VU and VR is 108°. From PV = VR, VW = PV, and VU = VR, it can be obtained that VU = VW, so triangle UVW is an isosceles triangle. Next trace the angles at point V: the angle from VW to VR is ∠PVR - ∠PVW = 90° - 60° = 30°, and then adding the 108° from VR to VU gives ∠UVW = 30° + 108° = 138°. Therefore the two base angles of isosceles triangle UVW are equal, each being (180° - 138°) / 2 = 21°. So ∠WUV = 21°.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a square PVRQ on the left, an equilateral triangle PVW drawn inside the square with base PV, and a regular pentagon VUTSR attached on the square side VR. Use the text to know the triangle is equilateral and the pentagon is regular. Since PV and VR are sides of the square, PV=VR. Since PVW is equilateral, VW=PV. Since VUTSR is a regular pentagon sharing side VR, VU=VR. Hence VU=VW, so triangle UVW is isosceles. Now angle-chase at V: in the equilateral triangle, angle PVW=60°. In the regular pentagon, the interior angle at V is 108°, between VU and VR. In the square, angle PVR=90°. Therefore the angle between VU and VW is 108°+90°-60°=138° when traced through the sector around V shown in the diagram. The two base angles of isosceles triangle UVW are then (180°-138°)/2=21°, so angle WUV=21°.

From the image, take V as the origin, let the square side length be 1, put P=(-1,0) and R=(0,-1), matching the horizontal top side PV and vertical side VR. Because triangle PVW is equilateral below PV, W=(-1/2,-√3/2). claims.source: Because PVW is an equilateral triangle, VW = PV

claims.claim: The interior angles of an equilateral triangle are 60°.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: Because PVW is an equilateral triangle, VW = PV, and ∠PVW = 60°

claims.claim: VW = PV。
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Because PVW is an equilateral triangle, VW = PV

claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: and ∠PVW = 60°

claims.claim: The sides of a regular pentagon are equal.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: Because VUTSR is a regular pentagon and shares side VR, VU = VR

claims.claim: Each interior angle of a regular pentagon is 108°.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: and each interior angle of a regular pentagon is 108°

claims.claim: VU = VR。
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Because VUTSR is a regular pentagon and shares side VR, VU = VR

claims.claim: At point V, the interior angle between VU and VR is 108°.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore, at point V, the interior angle between VU and VR is 108°

claims.claim: VU = VW。
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: From PV = VR, VW = PV, and VU = VR, it can be obtained that VU = VW

claims.claim: Triangle UVW is an isosceles triangle.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: So triangle UVW is an isosceles triangle

claims.claim: The angle from VW to VR is ∠PVR - ∠PVW.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The angle from VW to VR is ∠PVR - ∠PVW

claims.claim: The angle from VW to VR is 30°.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: ∠UVW equals the 30° from VW to VR plus the 108° from VR to VU.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Adding the 108° from VR to VU again, obtain ∠UVW = 30° + 108° = 138°

claims.claim: The two base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: Therefore the two base angles of isosceles triangle UVW are equal

claims.claim: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°.
claims.label: knowledge

claims.claim: Each base angle of isosceles triangle UVW is 21°.
claims.label: reasoning
reasoning
claims.source: So ∠WUV = 21°
